name: Murf AI (Murf API)
positioning: Murf is known for its voiceover studio and also sells a developer text-to-speech API (Falcon 2 for real-time streaming, Gen2 for studio-style rendering) alongside dubbing, translation and voice-changer APIs.

pricing.model: Pay-as-you-go by character (character packs bought up front), a free trial credit, and custom Enterprise plans with volume discounts. Prices differ by model.
pricing.headline: Falcon 2 (streaming model) is documented at 1 cent per 1,000 characters (USD 10 per 1M); Gen2 (non-streaming) is listed at USD 0.03 per 1,000 characters (USD 30 per 1M).

tiers.name: Falcon 2 (pay-as-you-go)
tiers.notes: From the Falcon 2 model docs page. The murf.ai/api marketing page instead gives a price of 1 cent per minute for Falcon; the two units are not reconciled on Murf's pages. Single-source: the Falcon 2 docs page; the live pricing page is JavaScript-rendered and could not be read.

tiers.name: Gen2 (pay-as-you-go)
tiers.notes: From Murf's Help Center 'Plans and Limits' page: buy 1,000 characters at USD 0.03, minimum purchase USD 2, optional autopay. Gen2 is available on the non-streaming Synthesize Speech endpoint and not on streaming. Single-source.

tiers.name: Free Trial
tiers.notes: Help Center: up to 1 API key; concurrency 5 and 1,000 requests/minute. API FAQ confirms 100,000 character credits with no expiry.

tiers.name: Enterprise / Custom
tiers.notes: Volume-based tiered discounts, reserved concurrency (docs state up to 10,000 concurrent calls on Falcon 2), data residency, 24x7 support. Sales-quoted.

pricing.freeTier: 100,000 characters of free API credit, no time limit (Murf API FAQ and Help Center).
promotions: Startup program: startups with fewer than 100 employees can get 50 million free characters for three months (Murf API FAQ; no end date stated for the programme itself).

voices.languages: 35 languages with 20+ speaking styles (vendor-stated); Falcon 2 voices can switch languages within a sentence ('MultiNative')
voices.customVoiceOrCloning: Instant voice cloning from a short sample and Professional voice cloning documented; Enterprise plan lists voice cloning on request.

streaming.vendorStatedLatency: Vendor-stated: Falcon 2 time-to-first-audio 'under 100ms' (docs); the murf.ai/api page separately states 55 ms model latency and sub-130 ms time to first audio for Falcon. WebSocket streaming supports Falcon; Gen2 is decommissioned for streaming.

compatibility.note: Murf documents its own request schema (api-key header, POST /v1/speech/stream with voice_id/model/locale fields), not the OpenAI /v1/audio/speech shape. No OpenAI-compatible mode appears in the docs index.

limits.concurrency: Docs rate-limit page: Falcon 2 free and pay-as-you-go 5 for US-East and 2 for global/regional endpoints; Gen2 5; Enterprise custom up to 10,000. Help Center page lists a different pay-as-you-go figure (15 concurrent, 10,000 requests/minute); the two pages disagree.

sdks: JavaScript SDK (mentioned on murf.ai/api; docs index lists a Python SDK)
Integrations: Zapier, Make, n8n, Pipecat, LiveKit, Agora

compliance.note: Self-attested on murf.ai/api: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, GDPR compliant and HIPAA compliant. The docs Enterprise page states SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, GDPR and CCPA alignment and a no-training covenant, but does not mention HIPAA.

strengths.claim: Falcon 2 is a streaming model aimed at voice agents, with data residency in several regions (US-East, US-West, India, Canada, Korea, UAE, Japan listed) and on-premise deployment documented.
Large catalogue stated at 150+ voices in 35 languages with 20+ styles and a multilingual voice capability.
Beyond TTS, the same API covers voice changer, translation and dubbing automation, useful for localisation workflows.
Enterprise documentation describes zero-retention mode (inline Base64 audio) and a no-training covenant.
Gen2 non-streaming endpoint offers custom pause tags, a pronunciation dictionary, audio-duration control and variations for studio-style voiceovers.

limitations.claim: Gen2 has been decommissioned for streaming; WebSocket streaming supports Falcon (Gen2 is not available for streaming), so the most customisable controls apply to non-streaming requests.
Default concurrency on free and pay-as-you-go plans is low (5 on US-East per the docs) and higher capacity needs an Enterprise plan.

stepsToMove: Create an API key in the Murf API dashboard; Murf authenticates with an 'api-key' header.

Swap the endpoint: HTTP streaming is POST https://global.api.murf.ai/v1/speech/stream (regional hosts such as in.api.murf.ai exist) and WebSocket streaming is wss://global.api.murf.ai/v1/speech/stream-input.
Replace Murf voice IDs (for example 'Gordon') and the model value ('falcon-2' or 'Gen2') with the target service's voice names.
Map output settings: Murf takes format (MP3, WAV, PCM and others), sampleRate (8000 to 48000) and locale fields.

Re-point any usage of Murf-specific features (pronunciation dictionary, pause tags, duration control, cloned voices) to equivalents, and keep inputs under Murf's 3,000-character request size if splitting logic exists.

bestFor: Teams that want one vendor for voiceover studio work plus a TTS, dubbing and voice-changer API, or voice-agent builders who need regional data residency and a large multilingual voice catalogue.
